   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;"><b>Note <em style="font: inherit;">17</em> </b>&#8212;<b> Stockholders</b>&#8217;<b> Equity</b>&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;"><i><span style="text-decoration: underline; ">Authorized Common Stock and Authority to Create Preferred Stock</span></i></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;">The Company has the authority to issue up to <ix:nonFraction id="c113575625" contextRef="i_2024-03-31" unitRef="Share" name="lvo:StockAuthorized" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">510,000,000</ix:nonFraction> shares, consisting of <ix:nonFraction id="c113575626" contextRef="i_2024-03-31" unitRef="Share" name="us-gaap:CommonStockSharesAuthorized" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">500,000,000</ix:nonFraction> shares of the Company&#8217;s common stock, $<ix:nonFraction id="c113575627" contextRef="i_2024-03-31" unitRef="USDPerShare" name="us-gaap:CommonStockParOrStatedValuePerShare" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">0.001</ix:nonFraction> par value per share, and <ix:nonFraction id="c113575628" contextRef="i_2024-03-31" unitRef="Share" name="us-gaap:PreferredStockSharesAuthorized" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">10,000,000</ix:nonFraction> shares of the Company&#8217;s preferred stock, $<ix:nonFraction id="c113575629" contextRef="i_2024-03-31" unitRef="USDPerShare" name="us-gaap:PreferredStockParOrStatedValuePerShare" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">0.001</ix:nonFraction> par value per share (the &#8220;preferred stock&#8221;).</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;">The Company <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>issue shares of preferred stock from time to time in <em style="font: inherit;">one</em> or more series, each of which will have such distinctive designation or title as shall be determined by the Company&#8217;s board of directors and will have such voting powers, full or limited, or <em style="font: inherit;">no</em> voting powers, and such preferences and relative, participating, optional or other special rights and such qualifications, limitations or restrictions thereof, as shall be stated in the resolution or resolutions providing for the issue of such class or series of preferred stock as <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>be adopted from time to time by the Company&#8217;s board of directors.&#160; The Company&#8217;s board of directors will have the power to increase or decrease the number of shares of preferred stock of any series after the issuance of shares of that series, but <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> below the number of shares of such series then outstanding.&#160; In case the number of shares of any series shall be decreased, the shares constituting such decrease will resume the status of authorized but unissued shares of preferred stock.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;">It is <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> possible to state the actual effect of the issuance of any shares of preferred stock on the rights of holders of the common stock until and unless the Company&#8217;s board of directors determines the specific rights of the holders of the preferred stock; however, these effects <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>include: restricting dividends on the common stock, diluting the voting power of the common stock, impairing the liquidation rights of the common stock, or delaying or preventing a change in control of the Company without further action by the stockholders.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;"><i><span style="text-decoration: underline; ">Stock Repurchase Program</span></i></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;">In <em style="font: inherit;"> December 2020, </em>the Company announced that its board of directors has authorized the repurchase of up to&#160;<span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c113575634">two</span>&#160;million shares of its outstanding common stock from time to time. In <em style="font: inherit;"> November 2022, </em>the Company announced that its board of directors has authorized it to expand its stock repurchase program by up to an additional $<ix:nonFraction id="c113575635" contextRef="i_2022-12-01" unitRef="USD" name="lvo:StockRepurchaseProgramIncreaseInAuthorizedAmount" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">2,000,000</ix:nonFraction>&#160;worth of shares of its common stock to be repurchased from time to time. The timing, price, and quantity of purchases under the program will be at the discretion of our management and will depend upon a variety of factors including share price, general and business market conditions, compliance with applicable laws and regulations, corporate and regulatory requirements, and alternative uses of capital. The program <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>be expanded, suspended, or discontinued by our board of directors at any time. Although our board of directors has authorized this stock repurchase program, there is <em style="font: inherit;">no</em> guarantee as to the exact number of shares, if any, that will be repurchased by us, and we <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>discontinue purchases at any time that management determines additional purchases are <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> warranted. We cannot guarantee that the program will be consummated, fully or all, or that it will enhance long-term stockholder value. The program could affect the trading price of our common stock and increase volatility, and any announcement of a termination of this program <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>result in a decrease in the trading price of our common stock. In addition, this program could diminish our cash reserves.&#160;The Company purchased <ix:nonFraction id="c113575638" contextRef="d_2023-04-01_2024-03-31" unitRef="Share" name="us-gaap:TreasuryStockSharesAcquired" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">1,639,125</ix:nonFraction>&#160;and <ix:nonFraction id="c113575639" contextRef="d_2022-04-01_2023-03-31" unitRef="Share" name="us-gaap:TreasuryStockSharesAcquired" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">2,220,914</ix:nonFraction>&#160;shares of its common stock under the stock repurchase program for the year ended <em style="font: inherit;"> March 31, 2024 </em>and <em style="font: inherit;">2023</em>, for a total of $<ix:nonFraction id="c113575642" contextRef="d_2023-04-01_2024-03-31" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:TreasuryStockValueAcquiredCostMethod" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">2.6</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million and $<ix:nonFraction id="c113575643" contextRef="d_2022-04-01_2023-03-31" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:TreasuryStockValueAcquiredCostMethod" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">2.2</ix:nonFraction> million, respectively. As of <em style="font: inherit;"> March 31, 2024, </em>the Company has up to $<ix:nonFraction id="c113575644" contextRef="i_2024-03-31" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:StockRepurchaseProgramRemainingAuthorizedRepurchaseAmount1" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">1.1</ix:nonFraction> million remaining to repurchase shares of its and/or PodcastOne&#8217;s outstanding common stock under the stock repurchase program, provided, that the Company&#8217;s management has authorized the repurchase of up to an additional $<ix:nonFraction id="c113575645" contextRef="i_2024-03-31" unitRef="USD" name="lvo:StockRepurchaseProgramIncreaseInAuthorizedAmount" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">2.5</ix:nonFraction> million worth of shares of the Company&#8217;s and/or PodcastOne&#8217;s outstanding common stock from time to time stock under the stock repurchase program, which $<ix:nonFraction id="c113575646" contextRef="i_2024-03-31" unitRef="USD" name="srt:StockRepurchaseProgramAuthorizedAmount1" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">2.5</ix:nonFraction> million is subject to approval of the Company&#8217;s board of directors.</p>

   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; text-align: justify; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;"><i><span style="text-decoration: underline; ">Series A Preferred Stock</span></i></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;">The Series A Preferred Stock is convertible at any time at a Holder&#8217;s option into shares of&#160;the Company&#8217;s common stock, at a price of $<ix:nonFraction id="c113575648" contextRef="i_2024-03-31_StatementClassOfStockAxis-SeriesAPreferredStockMember" unitRef="USDPerShare" name="us-gaap:PreferredStockConvertibleConversionPrice" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">2.10</ix:nonFraction> per share of common stock, bears a dividend of <ix:nonFraction id="c113575649" contextRef="d_2023-04-01_2024-03-31_StatementClassOfStockAxis-SeriesAPreferredStockMember" unitRef="Pure" name="us-gaap:PreferredStockDividendRatePercentage" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="2">12</ix:nonFraction>% per annum, is perpetual and has <em style="font: inherit;">no</em> maturity date. At the option of the Company, the dividend was to&#160;be paid in-kind until <em style="font: inherit;"> February 3, 2024, </em>and thereafter, the Holders had&#160;the option to select whether subsequent dividend payments shall be paid in kind or in cash; provided, that as long as any Series A Preferred Stock is held by the Harvest Funds (as defined below), Trinad Capital shall receive the dividend solely in kind. The Series A Preferred Stock shall have <em style="font: inherit;">no</em> voting rights, except as set forth in the Certificate of Designation or as otherwise required by law.</p>

The Company is required on or before <em style="font: inherit;"> August 3, 2024 (</em>the&#160;"Redemption Date&#8221;), and in any event if prior to the&#160;Redemption Date the Company consummated&#160;any financing transaction in which the Company, directly or indirectly, raised, in aggregate, gross proceeds of more than $<ix:nonFraction id="c113575653" contextRef="d_2023-04-01_2024-03-31_StatementClassOfStockAxis-SeriesAPreferredStockMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:ProceedsFromIssuanceOfMandatoryRedeemableCapitalSecurities" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">20,000,000</ix:nonFraction> of new capital, to purchase $<ix:nonFraction id="c113575654" contextRef="i_2024-03-31_StatementClassOfStockAxis-SeriesAPreferredStockMember" unitRef="USD" name="lvo:PreferredStockMaximumRedemptionAmount" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">5,000,000</ix:nonFraction> in aggregate of the then outstanding shares of Series A Preferred Stock held by the Harvest Funds (the &#8220;Mandatory Redemption Amount&#8221;) at the Redemption Price (the &#8220;Mandatory Redemption&#8221;). If the Optional Redemption Right is exercised up to the full $<ix:nonFraction id="c113575655" contextRef="i_2024-03-31_StatementClassOfStockAxis-SeriesAPreferredStockMember" unitRef="USD" name="lvo:PreferredStockMaximumRedemptionAmount" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">5,000,000</ix:nonFraction> amount, the Mandatory Redemption requirement was to be&#160;terminated; provided, that if the Optional Redemption Right is exercised in any amount less than $<ix:nonFraction id="c113575656" contextRef="i_2024-03-31_StatementClassOfStockAxis-SeriesAPreferredStockMember" unitRef="USD" name="lvo:PreferredStockMaximumRedemptionAmount" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">5,000,000</ix:nonFraction>, the Mandatory Redemption Amount was to&#160;be reduced by the amount that the Optional Redemption Right has been elected and exercised. $<ix:nonFraction id="c113575663" contextRef="i_2024-03-31_StatementClassOfStockAxis-SeriesAPreferredStockMember" unitRef="USDPerShare" name="us-gaap:PreferredStockConvertibleConversionPrice" scale="0"    <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;">In accordance with ASC <em style="font: inherit;">480,</em> the Company classified $<ix:nonFraction id="c113575678" contextRef="i_2024-03-31_StatementClassOfStockAxis-SeriesAPreferredStockMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:TemporaryEquityCarryingAmountAttributableToParent" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-6">5.0</ix:nonFraction> million of its Series A Preferred Stock as temporary equity due to the Company&#8217;s obligation to redeem $<ix:nonFraction id="c113575679" contextRef="i_2024-03-31_StatementClassOfStockAxis-SeriesAPreferredStockMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:TemporaryEquityCarryingAmountAttributableToParent" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-6">5.0</ix:nonFraction> million of the Series A Preferred Stock on or before&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">18</em> months after issuance for cash, which also contains a substantive conversion feature.&#160;The redemption feature was <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> deemed to be closely and clearly related to the equity-type host instrument.    <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;">In accordance with ASC <em style="font: inherit;">480,</em> the Company classified $<ix:nonFraction id="c113575687" contextRef="i_2024-03-31_StatementClassOfStockAxis-SeriesAPreferredStockMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:PreferredStockValue" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">16.2</ix:nonFraction> million of the Series A Preferred Stock as permanent equity in the financial statements as it was <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> subject to mandatory redemption at the option of the holder. The Company concluded that the Series A Preferred Stock is more akin to an equity-type instrument than a debt-type instrument, therefore the conversion features associated with the Series A preferred stock classified as permanent equity were deemed to be clearly and closely related to the host instrument and <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> a derivative under ASC <em style="font: inherit;">815.</em>&#160;Accordingly the Series A Preferred Stock was <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> accreted to the redemption amount in effect on the balance sheet date.</p>

   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; text-align: justify; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;"><i><span style="text-decoration: underline; "><em style="font: inherit;">2016</em> Equity Incentive Plan</span></i></p>

The stock options expire <span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c113575754">ten</span> years&#160;after the date of grant.</p>

   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;">The Company&#8217;s income tax provision can be affected by many factors, including the overall level of pre-tax income, the mix of pre-tax income generated across the various jurisdictions in which the Company operates, changes in tax laws and regulations in those jurisdictions, changes in valuation allowances on its deferred tax assets, tax planning strategies available to the Company, and other discrete items.</p>

The federal and state net operating loss carryforwards begin to expire on various dates beginning in <em style="font: inherit;">2028.</em> Of the $<ix:nonFraction id="c113575918" contextRef="i_2024-03-31_IncomeTaxAuthorityAxis-DomesticCountryMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:OperatingLossCarryforwards" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">147.9</ix:nonFraction> million of federal net operating loss carryforwards, $<ix:nonFraction id="c113575919" contextRef="i_2024-03-31_IncomeTaxAuthorityAxis-DomesticCountryMember" unitRef="USD" name="lvo:OperatingLossCarryforwardsSubjectToExpiration" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-6">66.0</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million was generated in tax years beginning before <em style="font: inherit;"> March 31, 2018 </em>and is subject to the <em style="font: inherit;">20</em>-year carryforward period (&#8220;pre-Tax Act losses&#8221;), the remaining $<ix:nonFraction id="c113575921" contextRef="i_2024-03-31_IncomeTaxAuthorityAxis-DomesticCountryMember" unitRef="USD" name="lvo:OperatingLossCarryforwardsNotSubjectToExpiration" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">81.9</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million (&#8220;post-Tax Act losses&#8221;) can be carried forward indefinitely but is subject to the <em style="font: inherit;">80%</em> taxable income limitation.</p>

   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;">The Company obtained $<ix:nonFraction id="c113575923" contextRef="i_2017-12-31_BusinessAcquisitionAxis-SlackerMember_IncomeTaxAuthorityAxis-DomesticCountryMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:OperatingLossCarryforwards" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">133.9</ix:nonFraction> million and $<ix:nonFraction id="c113575924" contextRef="i_2017-12-31_BusinessAcquisitionAxis-SlackerMember_IncomeTaxAuthorityAxis-DomesticCountryMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:TaxCreditCarryforwardAmount" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">1.5</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million of federal net operating loss and credit carryforwards, respectively, and $<ix:nonFraction id="c113575925" contextRef="i_2017-12-31_BusinessAcquisitionAxis-SlackerMember_IncomeTaxAuthorityAxis-StateAndLocalJurisdictionMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:OperatingLossCarryforwards" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">104.2</ix:nonFraction> million and $<ix:nonFraction id="c113575926" contextRef="i_2017-12-31_BusinessAcquisitionAxis-SlackerMember_IncomeTaxAuthorityAxis-StateAndLocalJurisdictionMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:TaxCreditCarryforwardAmount" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">1.7</ix:nonFraction> million of state net operating loss and credit carryforwards, respectively, through the acquisition of Slacker, Inc. in <em style="font: inherit;"> December 2017. </em>Utilization of these losses is limited by Section <em style="font: inherit;">382</em> and <em style="font: inherit;">383</em> of the Code in fiscal year end <em style="font: inherit;"> March 31, 2018 </em>and each taxable year thereafter. The Company updated its&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">382</em> study during the year ended <em style="font: inherit;"> March 31, 2024&#160;</em>to determine the applicable limitations. Upon the attainment of taxable income by the Company, management will assess the likelihood of realizing the tax benefit associated with the use of the carryforwards and will recognize the appropriate deferred tax asset at that time. The Company has estimated a limitation of the federal and state NOL of&#160;$<ix:nonFraction id="c113575930" contextRef="i_2017-12-31_BusinessAcquisitionAxis-SlackerMember" unitRef="USD" name="lvo:OperatingLossCarryforwardsLimitationsOnUseAmount" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">96.8</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million and $<ix:nonFraction id="c113575931" contextRef="i_2017-12-31_BusinessAcquisitionAxis-SlackerMember" unitRef="USD" name="lvo:TaxCreditCarryforwardLimitationsOnUseAmount" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">80.6</ix:nonFraction>, respectively. It is possible that the utilization of these NOL carryforwards and tax credits <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>be further limited.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;">The Company files tax returns as prescribed by the tax laws of the jurisdictions in which it operates. In the normal course of business, the Company is subject to examination by the federal and state jurisdictions where applicable. There are currently <em style="font: inherit;">no</em> pending income tax examinations. The Company&#8217;s tax years for <em style="font: inherit;">2018</em> and forward are subject to examination by the federal tax authorities and tax years for <em style="font: inherit;">2017</em> and forward are subject to examination by California tax authorities due to the carryforward of unutilized net operating losses.&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;">The Company&#8217;s policy is to record interest and penalties on uncertain tax provisions as income tax expense. As of <em style="font: inherit;"> March 31, 2024 </em>and <em style="font: inherit;">2023</em>, the Company has <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> accrued interest or penalties related to uncertain tax positions.</p>

   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;">As the ultimate realization of the potential benefits of a portion of the Company&#8217;s deferred tax assets is considered unlikely by management, the Company has offset the deferred tax assets attributable to those potential benefits through valuation allowances. Accordingly, the Company did <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> recognize any benefit from income taxes in the accompanying consolidated statements of operations to offset its pre-tax losses. The valuation allowance against deferred tax assets is $<ix:nonFraction id="c113575939" contextRef="i_2024-03-31" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:DeferredTaxAssetsValuationAllowance" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">41.8</ix:nonFraction> million and $<ix:nonFraction id="c113575940" contextRef="i_2023-03-31" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:DeferredTaxAssetsValuationAllowance" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-7">40.0</ix:nonFraction> million for the years ended <em style="font: inherit;"> March 31, 2024 </em>and <em style="font: inherit;">2023</em>, respectively.&#160;The valuation allowance increased by $<ix:nonFraction id="c113575942" contextRef="d_2023-04-01_2024-03-31" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:ValuationAllowanceDeferredTaxAssetChangeInAmount" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">1.8</ix:nonFraction> million for the year ended <em style="font: inherit;"> March 31, 2024</em>.</p>

   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;"><b>Note <em style="font: inherit;">19</em> </b>&#8212;<b> Business Segments and Geographic Reporting</b></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;">The Company determined its operating segments in accordance with ASC <em style="font: inherit;">280,</em> &#8220;Segment Reporting&#8221; (&#8220;ASC <em style="font: inherit;">280&#8221;</em>).</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;">Beginning in the <em style="font: inherit;">second</em> quarter of fiscal <em style="font: inherit;">2024,</em> management has determined that the Company has <span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c113576038">three</span>&#160;operating segments (PodcastOne, Slacker&#160;and Media Group). The Audio Group consist of the Company's PodcastOne and Slacker subsidiaries and the Media Group consist of the Company's&#160;remaining subsidiaries. As a result of the Spin-Out&#160;of PodcastOne,&#160;the Company&#8217;s chief operating decision maker (&#8220;CODM&#8221;) began to make decisions and allocate resources based on&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">three</em> operating segments of the business (PodcastOne, Slacker&#160;and Media group). The Company&#8217;s reporting segments reflects the manner in which its CODM reviews results and allocates resources. The CODM reviews operating segment performance exclusive of share-based compensation expense, amortization of intangible assets, depreciation, and other expenses (including legal fees, expenses, and accruals) related to acquisitions, associated integration activities, and certain other non-cash charges. As a result, the segment information for the prior periods has been recast to conform with the current period presentation.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;">The Company&#8217;s <em style="font: inherit;">three</em>&#160;operating segments are also consistent with its internal organizational structure, which is the way the Company assesses operating performance and allocates resources.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;"><i><span style="text-decoration: underline; ">Customers</span></i></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;">The Company has <em style="font: inherit;">one</em> external customer that accounts for more than <em style="font: inherit;">10%</em> of its revenue and accounts receivable. Such original equipment manufacturer (the &#8220;OEM&#8221;) provides premium Slacker service in its new vehicles. Total revenues from the OEM were $<ix:nonFraction id="c113576043" contextRef="d_2023-04-01_2024-03-31_MajorCustomersAxis-OriginalEquipmentManufacturerOemMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:RevenueFromContractWithCustomerExcludingAssessedTax" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">59.9</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million and $<ix:nonFraction id="c113576044" contextRef="d_2022-04-01_2023-03-31_MajorCustomersAxis-OriginalEquipmentManufacturerOemMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:RevenueFromContractWithCustomerExcludingAssessedTax" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">44.3</ix:nonFraction> million for the years ended <em style="font: inherit;"> March 31, 2024 </em>and <em style="font: inherit;">2023</em>, respectively. Total receivables from the OEM were <ix:nonFraction id="c113576047" contextRef="d_2023-04-01_2024-03-31_ConcentrationRiskByBenchmarkAxis-AccountsReceivableMember_ConcentrationRiskByTypeAxis-CustomerConcentrationRiskMember_MajorCustomersAxis-OriginalEquipmentManufacturerOemMember" unitRef="Pure" name="us-gaap:ConcentrationRiskPercentage1" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="2">42</ix:nonFraction>% and <ix:nonFraction id="c113576048" contextRef="d_2022-04-01_2023-03-31_ConcentrationRiskByBenchmarkAxis-AccountsReceivableMember_ConcentrationRiskByTypeAxis-CustomerConcentrationRiskMember_MajorCustomersAxis-OriginalEquipmentManufacturerOemMember" unitRef="Pure" name="us-gaap:ConcentrationRiskPercentage1" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="2">32</ix:nonFraction>% of total accounts receivable as of <em style="font: inherit;"> March 31, 2024 </em>and <em style="font: inherit;">2023</em>, respectively.&#160;</p>

  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><b><a id="item9a" title="item9a" href="#"></a>Item 9A. Controls and Procedures</b></p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;"><b>Evaluation of Disclosure Controls and Procedures</b>&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;">As of March 31, 2024, we carried out an evaluation, under the supervision and with the participation of our management, including our Chief Executive Officer (&#8220;CEO&#8221;) and&#160;Chief Financial Officer (&#8220;CFO&#8221;), of the effectiveness of our disclosure controls and procedures. Based upon that evaluation, our CEO and CFO have concluded that our disclosure controls and procedures were not effective as of March 31, 2024 because of material weaknesses in internal control over financial reporting, described in Management&#8217;s Annual Report on Internal Control Over Financial Reporting below.</p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;"><b>Management</b>&#8217;<b>s Annual Report on Internal Control Over Financial Reporting</b></p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;">Our management is responsible for establishing and maintaining adequate internal control over financial reporting. Internal control over financial reporting is defined in Rule&#160;13a-15(f) or 15d-15(f) promulgated under the Securities Exchange Act of 1934, as amended, as a process designed by, or under the supervision of, our principal executive and principal financial officers and effected by our board of directors, management and other personnel, to provide reasonable assurance regarding the reliability of financial reporting and the preparation of financial statements for external purposes in accordance with generally accepted accounting principles. Internal control over financial reporting includes those policies and procedures that (i)&#160;pertain to the maintenance of records that in reasonable detail accurately and fairly reflect the transactions and dispositions of the assets of our Company; (ii)&#160;provide reasonable assurance that transactions are recorded as necessary to permit preparation of consolidated financial statements in accordance with generally accepted accounting principles, and that receipts and expenditures of our Company are being made only in accordance with authorizations of our management and directors; and (iii)&#160;provide reasonable assurance regarding prevention or timely detection of unauthorized acquisition, use or disposition of our assets that could have a material effect on the consolidated financial statements.</p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;">Because of its inherent limitations, internal control over financial reporting may not prevent or detect misstatements. Projections of any evaluation of the effectiveness to future periods are subject to the risk that controls may become inadequate because of changes in conditions, or that the degree of compliance with the policies or procedures may deteriorate.</p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;">Our management, with the participation of our CEO and&#160;CFO, assessed the effectiveness of our internal control over financial reporting as of March 31, 2024, the end of our fiscal year. Our management based its assessment on criteria established in&#160;Internal Control - Integrated Framework&#160;(2013) issued by the Committee of Sponsoring Organizations of the Treadway Commission. Our management&#8217;s assessment included evaluation and testing of the design and operating effectiveness of key financial reporting controls, process documentation, accounting policies, and our overall control environment.</p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;">Based on our management&#8217;s assessment, our management has concluded that our internal control over financial reporting was not effective as of March 31, 2024 due to a material weakness&#160;that existed in our internal controls. Our management communicated the results of its assessment to the Audit Committee of our Board of Directors.</p>
  <p style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; margin: 0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;">A material weakness is a deficiency, or combination of deficiencies, in internal control over financial reporting, such that there is a reasonable possibility that a material misstatement of the Company&#8217;s annual or interim financial statements will not be prevented or detected on a timely basis. Based on management&#8217;s assessment of our internal control over financial reporting as of March 31, 2024, the following material weaknesses existed as of that date, specifically relating to the following control activities:</p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:32pt;">We did not maintain appropriately designed entity-level controls impacting the control environment, risk assessment procedures, and monitoring activities to prevent or detect material misstatements to the consolidated financial statements. These deficiencies were attributed to: (i) lack of structure and responsibility, insufficient number of qualified resources and inadequate oversight and accountability over the performance of controls, (ii) ineffective identification and assessment of risks impacting internal control over financial reporting, and (iii) ineffective evaluation and determination as to whether the components of internal control were present and functioning.</p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <div class="PGBK" style="width: 100%; margin-left: 0pt; margin-right: 0pt">
   <div class="PGNUM" style="text-align: center; width: 100%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: Times New Roman;">
     95
   </div>
   <hr style="PAGE-BREAK-AFTER: always; border: none; width: 100%; height: 2px; color: #000000; background-color: #000000"/>

     <div class="TOCLink hf-cell" style="width: 100%; display: inline-block; text-align: left;">

    </div>
   </div>

  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">In addition, as previously reported, material weakness&#160;specifically relating to the following control activity&#160;existed as of&#160;March 31, 2024:</p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <table border="0" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="width: 100%; text-indent: 0px;">
   <tbody>
    <tr style="vertical-align: top;">
     <td style="width: 36pt;">&#160;</td>
     <td style="width: 36pt;"> <p style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size: 10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">(i)</p> </td>
     <td style="width: auto;"> <p style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size: 10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">our controls relating to proper evaluation and accounting of certain features embedded in complex debt and equity instruments. Specifically, we did not have sufficient technical resources to appropriately identify and evaluate certain features that require instruments or features to be accounted for as liabilities remeasured at fair value.</p> </td>
    </tr>

   </tbody>
  </table>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;">Notwithstanding the material weakness&#160;discussed above, our management, including our CEO and&#160;CFO, concluded that the consolidated financial statements in this Annual Report fairly present, in all material respects, our financial condition, results of operations and cash flows for the periods presented, in conformity with GAAP.</p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;"><b>Remediation Plan for Material Weakness in Internal Control over Financial Reporting</b></p>
  <p style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; margin: 0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;">Our management, with oversight of the Audit Committee of our Board of Directors has identified and begun to implement several steps to remediate the material weakness&#160;described in this Item 9A and to enhance our overall control environment. During our fiscal year ending March 31, 2025, our management is committed to remediating such material weakness&#160;through continuing training and hiring of personnel, improving the timeliness of our accounting close process, and continuing to enhance our financial review controls. We are committed to ensuring that our internal controls over financial reporting are designed and operating effectively.</p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;">Although we intend to complete the remediation process as promptly as possible, we cannot at this time estimate how long it will take to remediate these material weakness. In addition, we may discover additional material weakness&#160;that require additional time and resources to remediate and we may decide to take additional measures to address the material weaknesses or modify the remediation steps described above. Until theses material weakness&#160;are remediated, we plan to continue to perform additional analyses and other procedures to ensure that our consolidated financial statements are prepared in accordance with GAAP.</p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;"><b>Attestation Report of the Independent Registered Public Accounting Firm</b></p>
  <p style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; margin: 0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;">This Annual Report does not include an attestation report of our independent registered public accounting firm regarding internal control over financial reporting. Because we are a smaller reporting company and a non-accelerated filer, our independent registered public accounting firm is not required to attest to or issue a report on the effectiveness of our internal control over financial reporting.</p>
  <p style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; margin: 0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;"><b>Changes in Internal Control over Financial Reporting</b></p>
  <p style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; margin: 0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;">During the fourth quarter of the fiscal year ended March 31, 2024, we continued the processes of evaluating the design and operating effectiveness of controls in place around new transaction cycles and will implement any remediations if necessary. Other than this, there have been no changes in our internal control over financial reporting, during the fourth quarter of the fiscal year ended March 31, 2024 that have materially affected, or are reasonably likely to materially affect, our internal control over financial reporting.</p>
  <p style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; margin: 0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;"><b>CEO and CFO Certifications</b></p>
  <p style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; margin: 0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;">Exhibits 31.1 and 31.2 to this Annual Report are the Certifications of our CEO and&#160;CFO, respectively. These certifications are required in accordance with Section 302 of the Sarbanes-Oxley Act (the &#8220;Section 302 Certifications&#8221;). This Item 9A. of this Annual Report, which you are currently reading, is the information concerning the Evaluation referred to above and in the Section 302 Certifications, and this information should be read in conjunction with the Section 302 Certifications for a more complete understanding of the topics presented.</p>
